title: Performance Assessment & Showcase
subtitle: Show the skills, show the portfolio, and say why you did it that way.
objectives: Explain what the TLE showcase asks for
Demonstrate a practical skill so it can be marked
Present the portfolio built in week 10
Explain a choice instead of only showing the result
Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

cards.title: Two halves: the skills and the portfolio
cards.text: One half is doing something with your hands. The other is the folder of work from week 10.

cards.title: Ten weeks, one tap each
cards.text: There is still a written half. This is your revision sheet for it.

cards.title: Every skill this term is demonstrable
cards.text: Making a bed, folding a shirt, sorting laundry, filing a sheet, naming a file. Any of them could be asked for.

question.text: What is the first step when demonstrating a practical skill?
options: Lay out everything you need before starting
Ask what the marks are for
question.explain: Preparation is visible and it is marked. Hunting for something mid-task is not.

cards.title: Slow enough to be seen
cards.text: An assessor has to watch each step happen. Doing it at your normal speed hides the steps you are being marked on.
points: **Say the step**, then do the step.

cards.title: A mechanic talks through the job
cards.text: Watch anyone good work on a car and they narrate it. Not for show — it is how you prove you knew the order.
points: **Naming the step** shows it was a decision.
**Ten extra words** per step is enough.

question.text: Finishing a demonstration means completing the task and resetting the space.
question.explain: The reset is part of finishing, in TLE as at home. Leaving it moves the job to someone else.

cards.title: Good place to pause
cards.text: Part 2 is the portfolio and talking about your work. Then a review of the whole term.

cards.title: You built this in week 10
cards.text: Gathered, chosen, renamed, arranged, captioned, backed up. This week you hand it over and talk about it.

cards.title: Six things before you submit
cards.text: Run this list once. Every item is something you can fix in ten minutes and cannot fix afterwards.

cards.title: The build tour, not the screenshot
cards.text: Anyone can show a finished base. What makes it worth watching is the person saying why each part is where it is.
points: **Explaining the choice is the other half.**
**Without the why**, it is just files.

cards.title: Name the piece you improved
cards.text: If you are asked one question about the portfolio, this is the answer that shows the most about you.

question.text: Which portfolio piece says the most about you?
options: The one you improved after feedback
The one with the highest mark
question.explain: Anyone can show a good piece. Showing a weak first attempt and what you did about it is harder.

cards.title: This is the subject you will actually use
cards.text: Folding, filing, naming, backing up, finishing a job. None of it stops being useful when the term ends.

question.text: A portfolio stored in one place only is finished and ready to submit.
question.explain: One copy is not a copy. A second copy somewhere else is the last step of building it.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Say the step, then do the step.**

quiz.text: What does it mean to give something a home?
options: It is stored out of sight
It has one place it always lives
quiz.explain: Week 1. If you have to think about where it goes, it will not go there.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the two-minute rule?
options: If it takes under two minutes, do it now
Spend two minutes tidying each day
quiz.explain: Week 1. Small jobs are what pile up into a job you cannot start.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the difference between a routine and a schedule?
options: A routine is an order of actions; a schedule attaches times
A routine is written down; a schedule is not
A schedule is only for work
quiz.explain: Week 2. A task without a time attached tends not to get done.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What is clutter?
quiz.explain: Week 3. A pile can be perfectly clean and still be clutter.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: You should organise a room first and declutter it afterwards.
quiz.explain: Week 3. The other way round. Tidy junk is still junk.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: How often should bedding be changed?
quiz.explain: Week 4. Most of what accumulates is invisible, so appearance is a poor guide.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What kind of room is easiest to fall asleep in?
quiz.explain: Week 4. Light, temperature and screens all change how quickly sleep arrives.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: Why should knitwear be folded rather than hung?
options: It stretches out of shape on a hanger
quiz.explain: Week 5. What to hang and what to fold is decided by the fabric, not by space.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: Why is laundry sorted before washing?
options: To stop dye transferring between items
quiz.explain: Week 5. One new red item can change the colour of a whole load.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: When should you say a supply is running low?
options: At the end of the month
When you open the last one
quiz.explain: Week 6. Opening the last one leaves time. Empty means someone has to fix it today.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: A routine works because each step cues the next one.
quiz.explain: Week 6. That is why the order has to stay the same. It removes the decision.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the main cost of a disorganised bag?
quiz.explain: Week 7. Nobody loses marks for a heavy bag.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: When should the school bag be packed?
quiz.explain: Week 7. Prepare when it is cheap. A school morning is the expensive part of the day.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What order should a filename use?
options: Date, then subject, then what it is
What it is, then the date
quiz.explain: Week 8. Written year-month-day, an alphabetical sort becomes a date sort.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: A copy in a second folder on the same laptop counts as a backup.
quiz.explain: Week 8. A backup has to survive whatever kills the original. Same machine, same accident.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the difference between archiving and deleting?
options: Archiving keeps the file but moves it out of the way
quiz.explain: Week 8. When you are unsure which to do, archive.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: When is a cooking job actually finished?
options: When the pan is off the heat
When the kitchen has been reset
quiz.explain: Week 9. Leaving the mess moves the rest of the job to someone else.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What turns a chore into a responsibility?
quiz.explain: Week 9. Reminders mean the job is still theirs.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: Which part of doing laundry do people most often fail?
quiz.explain: Week 9. Wet clothes left in the drum start to smell. The work is easy; the timing is the skill.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the first step in building a portfolio?
quiz.explain: Week 10. Two fast passes beat one slow careful one.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: Which three kinds of piece should a portfolio include?
options: Best, hardest, and one you improved
quiz.explain: Week 10. The improved one shows you can take a correction.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten TLE topics of the term

quiz.text: What should the second line of a caption say?
quiz.explain: Week 10. It is the line a reader actually learns from.
quiz.objective: Present the portfolio built in week 10

quiz.text: Why demonstrate a practical skill slowly?
options: The assessor has to see each step happen
quiz.explain: Normal speed hides the steps you are being marked on.
quiz.objective: Demonstrate a practical skill so it can be marked

quiz.text: Narrating each step while you demonstrate is worth doing.
quiz.explain: Naming the step shows it was a decision rather than something copied.
quiz.objective: Explain a choice instead of only showing the result

teacher.summary: Week 11 in TLE is a performance assessment and showcase rather than a written paper, and it has two halves: demonstrating a practical skill from the term, and handing over the portfolio built in week 10. The deck's most useful idea is that a demonstration has to be slow enough to be watched and narrated enough to show the order was a decision — most students lose marks by working at their normal speed in silence. The submission checklist is deliberately made of things fixable in ten minutes. The closing card makes the honest case that this is the subject whose content he will still be using in ten years.
discussion: Ask him to demonstrate one skill while narrating it, and time how much slower it is.
Ask him to run the six-item portfolio check before he submits anything.
Ask which piece he improved this term and what he changed.
Ask which habits from this term he intends to keep after the exam.
teacher.extension: Have him teach one of the skills to someone else, start to finish. Teaching it exposes every step he was skipping.
misconceptions: 'Doing it fast shows you know it.' Speed hides the steps being marked.
'The demonstration ends when the task is done.' Finishing includes resetting the space.
'A portfolio is a folder of files.' Without captions it is just files; the captions are the reasoning.
'One copy is enough.' A second copy elsewhere is the final step of building it.
